key_insight: π⁴ unifies 3D scene reconstruction and motion understanding in one model. It accepts a single RGB image, an unordered image collection, or a video to estimate scene geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, adding point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs.
problem_solved: Recovering both scene structure and movement from diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations, without requiring known camera parameters.
method: Use a geometry branch to reconstruct dense scene geometry, camera poses, and metric scale.
Condition a motion branch on the reconstructed geometry to predict image-space correspondences.
Lift correspondences into 3D using target-view geometry to support 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation.
impact: A unified model could simplify pipelines that otherwise combine separate reconstruction, camera estimation, and tracking systems. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no benchmark results, so performance gains cannot be assessed here.
visual_elements: Input-to-output diagram: single image, image collection, or video → π⁴ → geometry, camera poses, scale, tracks, and masks.
Two-branch architecture sketch showing geometry conditioning the motion branch.
Paired 2D and 3D views illustrating image correspondences lifted into spatial point tracks.
Video frames with colored moving-object masks and motion trails.
paper_title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
paper_authors: Yifan Wang, Weiguang Zhao, Ni Yang, Haoyu Guo, Junting Dong
